title: Jet-age air travel
summary: The British de Havilland Comet carried the first fare-paying jet passengers on 2 May 1952, but crashes grounded the early models. On 4 October 1958 BOAC's Comet 4 opened the first regular transatlantic jet service between London and New York, and before the month was out Pan American was flying Boeing 707s from New York to Paris; the 707, born of Boeing's jet-bomber work, entered commercial use that year, followed by the Douglas DC-8. As transatlantic ship passengers dwindled, shipping lines turned their liners to cruising.
